title: a bare `then X;` with no preceding succession to chain from
note: FOUND 2026-09-02 by a Fable advisory on examples/uav-isr.sysml, FIXED the same day. SysML chains successions: `first a then b; then c;` means a→b→c, a bare `then` continuing from the previous target. The mapper required BOTH endpoints, so every bare `then` was dropped SILENTLY — the UAV example wrote three and got one, with zero diagnostics. Bare `then` now chains; a `then` with nothing before it in the same scope is an error rather than a silent no-op, which is what this fixture pins.
